summary: The week's reading includes the story of Ruth, a Moabitess who shows steadfast love to her mother-in-law Naomi and becomes part of King David's lineage through her marriage to Boaz. In 1 Samuel, Hannah prays for a son, dedicates Samuel to the Lord's service, and Eli's corrupt priesthood contrasts with Samuel's faithful calling. The Philistines capture the ark of God, leading to divine judgment and eventual return to Israel.

people.name: Ruth
people.note: A Moabitess who marries Mahlon, remains loyal to Naomi after his death, and becomes the great-grandmother of King David through Boaz.

people.name: Naomi
people.note: Elimelech's wife and mother-in-law to Ruth and Orpah; returns to Bethlehem after her husband and sons die in Moab.

people.name: Boaz
people.note: A wealthy kinsman of Elimelech who redeems Ruth and marries her, continuing the lineage of David.

people.name: Hannah
people.note: Elkanah's wife who prays for a son, dedicates Samuel to the Lord's service, and sings a prayer of praise.

people.name: Eli
people.note: High priest at Shiloh whose sons Hophni and Phinehas are wicked; receives a prophecy of his house's destruction.

people.name: Samuel
people.note: Born to Hannah, raised in the temple, called by God as a prophet, and becomes a judge of Israel.

locations.name: Moab
locations.note: Where Elimelech's family goes during a famine; Ruth and Orpah marry Mahlon and Chilion there.

locations.name: Bethlehem
locations.note: Naomi and Ruth return here during barley harvest; Boaz's field is located here.

locations.name: Shiloh
locations.note: Location of the tabernacle where Eli and Samuel serve; Israelites worship here annually.

locations.name: Ashdod
locations.note: Philistines bring the ark here after capturing it, leading to plagues and destruction.

background: During the period of the Judges, Israelite society lacked centralized leadership, leading to familial and social challenges. Levirate marriage customs (deut. 25:5) required a relative to marry a childless widow to preserve her husband's lineage. Priests like Eli held significant religious authority, though corruption among his sons led to divine judgment. The ark symbolized God's presence, and its capture by the Philistines demonstrated the consequences of Israel's apostasy.
backgroundSource: footnote → Deut. 25:5; Come Follow Me manual

manualHighlights.note: Ruth and Hannah exemplify faith during trials; their stories show how the Lord turns tragedy into triumph and answers prayers.
The ark narrative teaches that obedience and repentance are more important than rituals; Israel's reliance on the ark without righteousness led to defeat.
Samuel's experience highlights the importance of learning to recognize the Lord's voice, as taught in D&C 6:22-23 and President Nelson's counsel on seeking revelation.
Boaz's role as a redeemer foreshadows Jesus Christ's Atonement, as both rescue individuals from despair and establish eternal covenants.
